A Multi-Faceted Approach to Office Security

The security needs of a modern office building are complex, ranging from preventing unauthorized access to ensuring employee safety and protecting sensitive corporate data. Security window film provides a versatile solution that addresses multiple risks, enhancing the overall safety and resilience of your corporate facility.

Key Security Applications in Office Buildings

  • Lobby and Ground-Floor Protection: The most accessible areas of an office building are the most vulnerable. Applying security film to lobby glass, entry doors, and all ground-floor windows provides a powerful deterrent against forced entry after hours.
  • Employee Safety: In the event of an accident, a natural disaster, or even an active threat scenario, security film holds broken glass in place, mitigating the risk of injury from flying shards and delaying entry for intruders.
  • Data Privacy: For executive offices or R&D labs, security film can be paired with privacy or cloaking films. For example, Casper Cloaking Film obscures LED screens from outside view, preventing corporate espionage.
  • Blast Mitigation: For high-risk corporate headquarters or government-adjacent offices, thicker gauge security films with attachment systems can help mitigate the devastating effects of a bomb blast, saving lives by containing flying glass.

A Smart, Unobtrusive Upgrade

Security film integrates seamlessly into your building's existing design. Our clear films provide protection without altering the building's appearance, making them an ideal choice for Class A office spaces where aesthetics are paramount. Combination films can also add energy savings and glare reduction, improving employee comfort and lowering operating costs—all while enhancing security.

This single upgrade can improve safety, increase energy efficiency, and enhance employee well-being, making it one of the most intelligent investments a building manager can make.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is security film installation disruptive to tenants?

We understand the need to minimize disruption in an active office building. Our professional teams work cleanly and efficiently, and we can schedule installations during evenings or weekends to avoid any impact on your tenants' operations.

Does the film meet any building code requirements?

Yes, safety and security films can be used to bring existing glazing up to code for impact safety standards (such as ANSI Z97.1 and CPSC 16 CFR 1201), which is often a more cost-effective solution than replacing the glass itself.

How does film compare to laminated glass for security?

Security film applied to existing glass offers a comparable level of protection to laminated glass but at a significantly lower cost and with much less disruption. It's the preferred retro-fit solution for security upgrades in existing buildings.
